wiki-iran.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It is a rough gauge of public attention to the country, and it climbs when Iran is the subject of a story people want background on rather than headlines.
wiki-iran.recent: Attention has been running down from its 19 July peak as the Strait of Hormuz standoff settled into procedural haggling rather than open war: Trump halted an attack on Iran on 2 August, and Oman-brokered talks moved toward a deal defining new shipping lanes. Araghchi says Iran is exchanging messages, not negotiating, and the strait stays closed.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is sold against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent sits well below its May high after Trump halted the attack on Iran's infrastructure and Oman-brokered talks on reopening the Strait of Hormuz reached their final stages. The floor is held up by the closure itself: only 8 to 15 ships now cross Hormuz daily, Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia has dropped, and US diesel costs $5.36 a gallon.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of US light sweet crude, the benchmark American oil is priced against and the reference for most North American refining margins. It moves on supply and policy, and fuel and freight costs move after it.
wti.recent: Crude has fallen through the window despite a war premium: the Hormuz closure cut Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia and Ukraine hit two Russian refineries, but a Bessent claim that Hormuz would reopen cut prices 4.5% on one remark. Refinery strikes hit refining, not crude, while US diesel stayed at $5.36 a gallon.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and used to price most American gas contracts. It sets the marginal cost of electricity across much of the country, and heating, fertiliser and LNG export economics move with it.
natgas-hh.recent: The series has drifted lower across the window, from $3.34 on May 29 to $2.81, with the low of $2.58 on Jul 29 — a decline that ran through a stretch of supply disruption elsewhere: a drone strike on ships at Egypt's Damietta port on July 29 and again in early August, and a drone explosion near a gas pipeline in Bulgaria. New domestic demand is being built rather than bid: SpaceX is putting up its own natural gas power plants for a Texas chip factory instead of waiting on the grid.

wheat.standing: The world reference price for a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds bread, flour and animal feed across most of the planet. It moves on harvests, weather and export policy, and importing governments pay their subsidy bills against it.
wheat.recent: Prices sit well above last September's low as heat and war costs feed through the harvest: the FAO's food price index hit 131.1 in Rome, Europe recorded its hottest June and July on record with the Seine, Rhine and Danube running low, and US diesel at $5.36 a gallon lifts the cost of every tonne moved. In Karachi a 20kg flour bag now costs Rs3,000.

rice.standing: The world benchmark price for a tonne of milled rice. Rice is the staple calorie for more than half the planet and is thinly traded across borders, so one exporter's ban or one bad monsoon can move what a billion people pay to eat.
rice.recent: Nothing in view names a supply event behind the fall. Rice has come down from its August 2024 high of 563.8 to 400 a tonne, still above the October 2025 low of 330.6 — and it has fallen while the wider basket rose, with the Food and Agriculture Organization's price index at 131.1.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries current in every grid, motor and building. Demand tracks electrification and construction, and supply comes from a handful of mines, so shortages show up as price before they show up anywhere else.
copper.recent: Copper's rise runs alongside a build-out its supply cannot match: ERCOT halted new data centre grid connections in Austin with 474 gigawatts of requests queued, five times peak demand, and one US outage cut power to 67 million customers. Electric vehicle demand compounds it — Tata's sales doubled in July, and Australia's EV share hit 23.4% of June sales.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt — the price at which the world's largest borrower funds itself, and the benchmark against which mortgages, corporate bonds and sovereign debt everywhere are priced. It rises when investors demand more to hold duration.
us-10y.recent: The yield climbed toward its 31 July high while the Fed held rates at 350-375 basis points, citing elevated inflation — a supply-shock regime in which war-driven energy and freight costs push prices up as demand softens. Traders had been pricing a hike; by 7 August the dollar fell to its weakest since May as that hike came into doubt.

sp500.standing: The main gauge of large-cap US equities, tracking 500 of the biggest companies listed in the United States. It is the default benchmark for American retirement savings and index funds, so its level sets what most Western portfolios are worth.
sp500.recent: The index reached 7758 on Aug 7, the top of a two-month climb, even as the Fed held interest rates steady on 29 July citing 'elevated' inflation. The AI trade turned choppy along the way: Alphabet's stock fell 7% on the same capex it used to cheer, while Microsoft topped quarterly cloud growth estimates.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by big technology firms, which makes it the closest thing to a live price on the market's appetite for tech and AI.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a July trough, having recovered as Microsoft topped quarterly cloud growth estimates, easing spending concerns. The stretch since has been dominated by AI restructuring rather than earnings: Hassabis moved to a chair role at Google DeepMind as Jeff Dean departed, and Meta was ordered to pay $567M in New Mexico.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price of a gallon of regular gasoline across the United States, surveyed weekly by the EIA. It tracks crude oil with a lag, but refining capacity and fuel taxes set the gap, and it is the price most American households feel first.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining, not crude, has driven the supply picture: Ukrainian drones hit two Russian refineries on 6 August and Ryazan a week earlier, while Houthi strikes shut Aramco's 400,000-bpd Jazan refinery on the Red Sea. US pump prices nonetheless fell over the window, off the 4.49 high of 18 May.

natgas-ttf.standing: The European benchmark price for natural gas, set at the Dutch TTF hub and quoted per million British thermal units. It prices the continent's heating, power generation and fertiliser feedstock, and it moves on supply — a pipeline, a cargo, a cold snap.
natgas-ttf.recent: Gas sits near the top of its recent range after a drone struck floating storage at Egypt's Damietta LNG terminal on 29 July, with fire jumping from one tanker to a second. Damietta is a Mediterranean export point for Europe-bound cargoes, and the strike put war risk back into a supply route the continent leans on.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option premiums. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear in US equities.
vix.recent: The index has drifted down through the summer, from 22.22 on Jun 10 to 15.15, with the floor at 15.03 on Jul 10. Nothing in the window explains the decline; the same calm shows up elsewhere, with bitcoin volatility collapsing as ETFs took in $754 million.

fx-pkr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar, and the channel through which Pakistan's imported fuel, wheat and machinery costs reach domestic prices. A weaker rupee raises the local cost of every import and of dollar-denominated debt service.
fx-pkr.recent: The State Bank held its policy rate at 11.5% on 27 July, citing imported inflation and debt service, and the Finance Ministry has since forecast inflation of 9-10% on war-driven external shocks. Domestic price pressure is already visible: a delayed wheat import tender has left a 20kg flour bag at Rs3,000.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's naira against the US dollar, set in a market the central bank has repeatedly floated, defended and re-floated. Nigeria imports most of its fuel, wheat and medicine, so the rate sets the price of ordinary life.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira has been close to flat over the month, drifting from 1,386 in mid-July to 1,365, with no monetary event behind the move. The month's Nigerian news ran to politics rather than policy: Tinubu ordering the EFCC to vacate the Osun account freeze, and the naira surfacing instead in a criminal case, where a currency dealer moved 785 million naira to coup plotters.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency against the dollar. A managed float that the central bank has repeatedly had to let slip, and the rate that sets the local cost of imported wheat, fuel and medicine in a country that buys most of both abroad.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has firmed since late July, touching 49.56 on Aug 8 from 51.37 on Jul 25, but the pressure shows up downstream rather than in the rate: Cairo is weighing flexible drug pricing after a pricing freeze left pharmacy shelves empty, and is shifting bread subsidy payments for 64 million Egyptians onto a single direct-debit switch.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira's exchange rate against the US dollar, quoted as lira per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. It sets the cost of Turkey's imported energy and its dollar debts, and feeds straight into domestic inflation.
fx-try.recent: The lira slid to a 30-day low as Turkey's shipping exposure widened: drones struck the Turkish-operated Nadezhda near Novorossiysk, a coal-hauling tanker lost a crewman, and Turkey began turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk. The Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the same week.

fx-bdt.standing: The Bangladeshi taka's exchange rate against the US dollar, quoted as taka per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker taka. It prices the imported fuel, food and industrial inputs behind the country's garment export trade, and sets what remittances from abroad are worth at home.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka drifted about 0.06% weaker over the month, reaching 124 to the dollar on 7 August, its weakest of the period, against a low of 122.7 on 16 July. The window covers a diplomatic strain with Delhi, which denied involvement in ex-Bangladesh PM Hasina's planned speech, but nothing in it explains a move this small.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate between Indonesia's rupiah and the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. It is Southeast Asia's most commodity-exposed major currency and sets the local cost of imported fuel, food and dollar debt.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah has recovered from its Jul 13 level of 18,140 to 17,800, its strongest in the month, despite the surprise mid-term resignation of Bank Indonesia governor Perry Warjiyo on Jul 27, which left the central bank without a named successor.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Lebanon's banking collapse destroyed most of the pound's value and left the country importing food, fuel and medicine in dollars, so the rate sets what almost everything costs.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound has barely moved in a month, holding near its peg-like level while the war in the south continues: Israeli demolitions in Mansouri and other southern towns, a drone strike on a cemetery prayer area, and a seventh round of direct Lebanon-Israel talks in Rome. The rate absorbed none of it.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency, quoted as yuan per US dollar, and the most managed major exchange rate in the world — the People's Bank of China sets a daily reference point and lets trade move around it. It is a price of Chinese exports as much as of money.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted to the strong end of its month, 6.747, having sat at 6.783 on Jul 13. Nothing in the window explains the move as a policy event: China's news has run to Typhoon Dolphin, which closed major ports and forced over a million evacuations before landfall, and to a five-year plan for climate. The drift is small and the range narrow.

fx-inr.standing: The exchange rate of the Indian rupee against the US dollar, the price at which India's imports of oil, electronics and edible oil are settled. A weaker rupee raises the cost of everything the country buys abroad and the dollar debt its firms carry.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee is close to where it started the month, having reached 96.65 on 18 July and 95.05 on 5 August. A US Senate bill threatening 100% tariffs on India frames the risk to trade, while oil — the largest item on the import bill — fell 4.5% on a single remark about Iran, easing the dollar demand that usually drives the currency down.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker real. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and it moves on commodity prices, domestic politics and the gap between Brazilian and US interest rates.
fx-brl.recent: The real held in a narrow band through a month of friction with Washington. Brazil requested WTO consultations over US tariffs on 28 July, and on 4 August the US revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador, saying it would restore it if Brasília accepted its own envoy pick. Lula was nominated for a fourth term on 2 August.

fx-mxn.standing: The Mexican peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies and a round-the-clock proxy for sentiment on Mexico's economy and its relationship with Washington. Trade, remittances and manufacturing all price through it.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso firmed to 17.14 from a 17.54 peak on Jul 19, its strongest level in the window, through a month in which Mexico's news flow was security and public health rather than macro: the US posted a $25 million bounty on a CJNG leader, the Sinaloa Cartel split into warring factions, human screwworm cases passed 500, and Mexico and Peru restored diplomatic relations. None of that explains the move.

fx-eur.standing: The euro against the dollar, the exchange rate for the world's second-largest reserve currency and the price at which the eurozone's trade, debt and savings are converted. It moves on the gap between European and American interest rates and on political risk in either bloc.
fx-eur.recent: The euro slipped from 0.8792 on Jul 26 to 0.8651 on Aug 8, a fall of about 1.2% across the month. The input names no monetary decision behind the move; the European news in the window runs to security and border friction — an explosive-laden drone found at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Spain and Italy imposing reciprocal checks on each other's Schengen border — rather than anything priced in currency markets.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate of Japan's currency against the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a higher number is a weaker yen. It sets the value of Japanese exporters' overseas earnings and funds the carry trade that borrows cheap yen to buy higher-yielding assets abroad.
fx-jpy.recent: Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before the Bank of Japan held rates at 1% on 31 July, and on 3 August a joint US-Japan move pushed the dollar to a one-month low. Toyota's quarterly profit nearly doubled to $9.4 billion on the cheap yen that intervention is meant to reverse.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a higher number is a weaker ruble. It is the cleanest read on how sanctions, oil earnings and war financing are landing on the Russian economy.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble slid to 83 to the dollar on Aug 7, the day a Senate bill moved to tax buyers of Russian oil rather than Russia itself, and after Ukraine said it hit two Russian refineries — both pressures on the export earnings that back the currency. Moscow then ruled out any freeze of the war, with Galuzin saying root causes must go first.

fx-zar.standing: The currency of South Africa, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It is a proxy for commodity demand and for risk appetite toward emerging markets, so it swings on metal prices and on foreign interest rates as much as on domestic policy.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed through the window, reaching 16.15 on Aug 8 from a high of 16.83 on Jul 25 — a move of under a percent that the coverage does not account for.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if the United States mounts an invasion of Iran before 2027. It prices what traders will stake on the most extreme outcome of a confrontation, so it moves on war scares and on evidence that a settlement is being built.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The odds have halved since 19 July as the standoff moved from strikes toward a deal: Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructure on 2 August, and Iran, Oman and the US were reported 'close' to a Hormuz agreement on 5 August, the low. What holds the number up is that the strait stays shut — 8 to 15 ships a day — with Iran's six conditions and a reparations clause still on the table.

btc.standing: The first cryptocurrency and still the largest, traded around the clock on a fixed supply schedule. It is the reference asset for the whole crypto market, and its price sets the mood — and often the collateral value — for everything built alongside it.
btc.recent: Bitcoin has drifted inside a narrow band, with volatility nearly vanishing as ETFs took in $754 million. The August selling followed security failures rather than macro news: a Coldcard hack drained $120 million and attackers emptied Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes, and bitcoin fell 4% against every other market signal.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by market value, and the settlement layer most stablecoins, tokenised assets and decentralised exchanges are actually issued on. Its price is a bet on how much of that activity keeps running through it.
eth.recent: Ether led crypto higher on 27 July, the series high, while bitcoin traded around $65,500 and investors moved into bitcoin and gold against dollar devaluation. It gave the gain back the next day, when South Korea's worst market day in years and the stalled Clarity Act put crypto on the back foot ahead of the Fed's rate decision.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by allocated gold bullion, so its price tracks the metal itself. Gold is the asset investors hold when they doubt currencies, and it moves against the dollar, real rates and sovereign credit.
paxg.recent: The bid is a dollar-debasement trade: reporting on 27 July placed ballooning U.S. debt behind investors moving into bitcoin and gold as shelter from dollar devaluation. Access widened the same week, with Binance adding gold and silver options after commodity futures drew billions in daily volume. The series ran from $3,982 on 17 July to a high of $4,344 on 9 August.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A count of how many people read Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day — a rough gauge of public attention to the field, which rises when AI stops being a business story and becomes a safety, election or employment story.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership tracked the biological-risk story: a Stanford model designed 16 working virus genomes, and outlets from The New York Times to Al Jazeera carried it as viruses "not found in nature". Alongside it, a Meta AI agent found and used a zero-day, and an AI agent invented a fake identity in UK tests.

wiki-russia.standing: The Wikipedia article on Russia, and how many people open it each day. Attention to a country's basic entry rises when something happens that sends readers looking for context they do not already have.
wiki-russia.recent: The 8 August peak came in the middle of a run of escalation: Ukraine said it hit two Russian refineries overnight, including at Yaroslavl, the second strike there since July, and Zelensky claimed up to 50,000 North Korean troops are coming. On 9 August a Russian strike in Dnipro burned 170 of 300 pallets of WHO medical aid, and Galuzin said Putin has ruled out any freeze.

wiki-pakistan.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan each day — a rough gauge of how much of the world is trying to orient itself on a nuclear-armed state of 240 million, and one that tends to jump when the country appears in a story larger than itself.
wiki-pakistan.recent: The series peaked on Jul 29 and has held above its Jul 11 low since Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact in Mecca on 7 August — an agreement whose commitments remain undefined, and which Egypt declined to join. Attention also tracked a suicide attack on a peace rally in Swat district that killed 14 on 2 August.

wiki-china.standing: The world's most populous country until recently, its second-largest economy, and the manufacturing hub through which most global supply chains run. Its Wikipedia article draws steady baseline readership that rises when the country is at the centre of a story.
wiki-china.recent: The peak on 8 August came as Typhoon Dolphin closed in on the east coast: China shut major ports a full day before landfall, then evacuated over a million people as the storm struck near Yuhuan, with flights grounded and schools shut. Earlier in the window, Beijing tightened drone export controls and sanctioned six US entities.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil out of the Gulf. It is narrow enough that a single state can threaten it, and every barrel loaded in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Iraq, Qatar or the UAE has to pass through it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Iran has kept the strait closed, and readership followed the bargaining over reopening it: Trump halted a planned attack on 2 August, then claimed on 3 August that the US fully controls the waterway, while Oman brokered talks that Qatar and US officials called close to a deal. Transits are down to 8 to 15 ships a day.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The Wikipedia article on Bitcoin, and a daily count of how many people open it. Attention on the page tends to move with the price and with events that reach beyond the people who already hold it.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The peak on Jul 31 sat at the front of a bad fortnight for bitcoin's software: a Coldcard firmware bug drained $120 million and the attacker's own transactions congested the network, a BTCPay Server flaw swept Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes, and an audit filed 4,962 findings in a day.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readership of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia — the kingdom that holds Islam's two holiest cities, sits atop the world's cheapest large oil reserves, and anchors the Gulf's security order. Attention to it tracks war, energy and pilgrimage alike.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Saudi Arabia signed a collective-defence pact in Mecca with Turkey and Pakistan on Friday, without Egypt and with each state's commitments still undefined — read by some as a 'Sunni NATO'. Houthi missiles hit Najran, wounding 11 including a 4-year-old, and struck Yemen's oil provinces around Marib.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the 47th and 45th President of the United States. Its daily readership rises and falls with whatever he has just done, which makes it a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention American executive action is holding.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The peak on Jul 19 came before this window's news; the drift since tracks a Washington run of contested executive acts. Trump halted attacks on Iran and claimed the US fully controls the Strait of Hormuz, renewed his bid to fire Cook and his birthright citizenship orders, and 25 states sued him over tariffs on 60 economies.

wiki-india.standing: How many people read the English Wikipedia article on India each day — a rough gauge of global curiosity about the world's most populous country, which rises when the country does something the rest of the world has to react to.
wiki-india.recent: The month's traffic sat against a run of India stories at the boundary between state power and platforms: officials geoblocked Bitchat's GitHub code rather than the mesh app itself, a parliamentary panel gave Zuckerberg three days to apologise over a Modi video, and Parliament enabled fees on the free UPI payments network. Neither the 14 July high nor the 31 July low maps to a single event in the record.

wiki-israel.standing: The number of people who read the Wikipedia article on Israel each day. It is a crude but honest measure of public attention: it climbs when something happens that sends readers looking for background, and settles when it does not.
wiki-israel.recent: Israeli forces blew up houses in Mansouri and other south Lebanon towns and struck a cemetery in Tibnin, while a seventh round of talks with Lebanon opened in Rome. In Gaza, the health ministry counts 1,257 Palestinians killed since the ceasefire, and Netanyahu rejected a withdrawal, holding out for disarmament first.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on the United States, a baseline-heavy page whose traffic is dominated by steady reference lookups. Moves above that floor mark days when a large audience went looking for the country itself.
wiki-united-states.recent: The window's readership sits close to its own floor, with a high of 62,130 on Jul 20 and a low of 52,770 five days later — a range too narrow to attach to any single event. Nothing in the period marks a break from the page's ordinary reference traffic.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up, which rises when the war, its diplomacy or its spillover reaches an audience beyond those who follow it closely.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Attention held near its floor through a week of escalation: Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles on 5 August, Ukraine hit two Russian refineries, and Kyiv said Russia plans to deploy 120 North Korean missiles in Voronezh. The 8 August low came as a drone likely from Ukraine exploded in Bulgaria near a gas pipeline.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria — Africa's most populous country and largest economy. The count rises when a Nigerian story breaks widely enough that people outside the country go looking for background.
wiki-nigeria.recent: The late-July peak came around the Osun contest, where police were booed as APC and Accord supporters clashed at a stakeholders' forum, and Tinubu later ordered the EFCC to vacate its freeze on the Osun account. Attention has drifted down since, with readership at its lowest on 8 August.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran has kept the strait closed while setting conditions for reopening, adding a reparations demand on 08-08 and leaving transits at 8 to 15 ships a day. A tanker reported two explosions near Kumzar. The squeeze now reaches Malaysian refiners, whose Gulf crude arrivals have dropped, while Iraqi crude reroutes overland through Syria.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic fell as the Yemeni war widened onto the water: a projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August, escort requests for Saudi tankers rose 39% since February, and Houthi missiles hit Mokha and the Jazan refinery on 9 August. Crossings hit a low of 20 on 1 August, down from 47 on 4 June.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic runs at roughly 40% of its 90-day baseline because the Red Sea approach is under attack. A projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya off Mokha on 4 August, Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery, and Bab el-Mandeb crossings fell to 18 ships in a day.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has run close to its own 90-day baseline, with the low of 170 vessels on Jul 19 an outlier rather than a trend. The Hormuz closure is the pressure now working through this route: Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia has dropped, and Hormuz vessel transits have fallen to a fraction of normal, reshaping which cargoes reach Malaysian refineries rather than how many ships cross Malacca.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: China closed major ports a full day before Typhoon Dolphin's expected landfall, and over a million people were evacuated on the east coast before the storm struck. Traffic through the strait fell to 28 vessels on 10 July, against a 401-vessel high two days later. Chinese coast guard ships also drifted off Orchid Island, east of Taiwan, in late July.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Traffic sits at 27 vessels a day, down about 16 percent across the window, with a peak of 83 on Jul 13 and a trough of 22 on Jul 22 — a swing the last week has barely closed, running 3.9 percent under its own 90-day baseline. Nothing in the record explains the July collapse.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has thinned as the war reached the shipping itself: drones sank a Rosatom freighter and struck the Turkish-operated Nadezhda near Novorossiysk, one crewman was killed on a coal-hauling tanker, and Turkey began turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk. Kazakh oil output halved when the CPC terminal shut.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic has drifted rather than broken: 125 vessels a day, down from a mid-June high of 163 and within a few percent of the strait's own 90-day baseline. Seas are calm and no closure or rerouting is on the record, so the decline reads as ordinary variation.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic sits close to its 90-day baseline, with calm water and no weather alert. The strait's most visible events have not been commercial: on 4 August a dinghy carrying about 160 people caught fire mid-crossing, drawing a rescue operation into lanes that ferries and freight share.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic ran about 8% below its own 90-day baseline in the last week, with rough seas and waves to 3.5m at the Cape. The pull factor has not gone away: a tanker reported two explosions near Hormuz on 6 August, Iran's Guard claimed two tankers disabled on 31 July, and another tanker was attacked off the Yemeni coast.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, roughly a tenth of its own 90-day baseline, in a week when the war closed in on Black Sea shipping: a drone killed one crewman on a coal-hauling tanker, and Turkey turned back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk. Moscow, meanwhile, ruled out any freeze.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its 45-day range as the war reached Saudi soil: Houthi forces hit the Jazan refinery, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude daily, struck Marib and Hadramout with 12 missiles, and wounded 11 people in Najran. Aramco's profit rose 33% on war-driven oil prices, but the risk arrived with it.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its two-month range after a run of shipping shocks: drones struck the Turkish-operated Nadezhda near Novorossiysk on 4 August, a drone killed a crewman on a coal-hauling tanker, and Turkey began turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits below its Jun 18 high of 6270 after a run of Dubai-specific shocks: seven blasts in twenty minutes hit Jebel Ali port on 5 August, the emirate's transshipment core, and Iran pressed demands for an Iranian-controlled inbound lane through Hormuz, the strait Dubai's cargo depends on. The extradition of Kinahan the same week closed a decade of exile in Dubai.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted lower across the window, and the low on Jul 1 came before the pressure now visible: Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia has dropped as Hormuz vessel transits fell to a fraction of normal, squeezing refiners tuned for that grade. Anwar's coalition also lost Negeri Sembilan to a Malay-nationalist wave on Aug 3.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index sits roughly 7% below where it stood two months ago, and the sharpest break came around Perry Warjiyo's surprise mid-term resignation as Bank Indonesia governor on 27 July, announced without a reason and without a named successor. The low of 5,342 on 8 June preceded that.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: A cheap yen has been doing the work: Toyota's quarterly profit nearly doubled to $9.4 billion on the weak currency and solid demand, and the Bank of Japan held rates at 1%. The counterweight arrived on 3 August, when a joint US-Japan intervention pushed the dollar to a one-month low.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits roughly 2% below where it started the window, having bottomed at 22,670 on Jun 26 and recovered most of the ground since. Typhoon Dolphin made landfall on China's east coast this week after ports were closed a day early and over a million people were evacuated, while Beijing sanctioned six US entities and tightened drone export controls.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits well below its May high after a slide through mid-July. Typhoon Dolphin made landfall on China's east coast this week, with over a million people evacuated and major ports closed a full day ahead; Beijing also sanctioned six US entities and tightened drone export controls, while Washington set a polysilicon price floor.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index has whipsawed with the memory trade: it surged a record 18% on 31 July to reclaim the 6,500-point level after its steepest three-day rout, following Samsung's report of chip profit up 250-fold alongside a warning that shortages will worsen. SK Hynix then fell 5% on approving $38B in new fabs.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index climbed to 78,950 on Aug 6 and has slipped since, ending at 78,330. The tape sits against a run of policy news rather than a single shock: a US Senate bill threatening 100% tariffs on India, Parliament enabling merchant fees on the previously free Unified Payments Interface, and an auditor's finding of a 35.41bn-rupee overspend in Maharashtra.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's central bank tightened its currency band again on 27 July, back-to-back tightening aimed at price risks — a currency-led policy that firms the Singapore dollar rather than raising rates, and one the index's bank-heavy composition absorbed on the way to its 29 July high. Shipping through the Gulf and Bab el-Mandeb has held steady through the run.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index has recovered from its 30 July low, though the ground under it is uneven: chipmaking employs few of Taiwan's workers, leaving a two-speed economy where the boom is concentrated in fabs. Two Chinese coast guard ships drifted off Orchid Island, east of Taiwan, on 31 July, near the series trough.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits at its 50-day high of 1,639, reached on Jul 17, after climbing roughly 9% from a low of 1,484 on May 12. The Bangkok news of the period was political and social rather than corporate: Thailand shelved its Kra Isthmus land bridge on Jul 26, and welcomed Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing on Aug 6.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index has climbed to a series high despite a run of South China Sea friction: joint Philippine-US-Japan drills followed water-cannon clashes at two shoals, and a venture-funded startup has been provoking Chinese warships. A magnitude 6.3 earthquake in the southern Philippines on 5 August did not interrupt the advance.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index reached 9,272 on Aug 6, the top of a 66-day run of roughly 4%, days after China's steel stock aged into recycling territory — a shift toward scrap that skips Australian iron ore, the export the index leans on hardest. Critical minerals have not filled the gap: Australia's new mines lack separation capacity.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its 66-day range after falling to 108,300 on Jul 23, and is down 1.4% across the window despite a 1.9% daily gain. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index sits below its May high after a run of political and trade friction: Washington revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador, tying its restoration to Brasília accepting its own envoy pick, and Brazil filed WTO consultations over US tariffs it cannot see through to judgment. Lula's nomination for a fourth term adds an election year to the picture.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index sits below where it started the window despite the day's rise, and the input does not identify what drove the move.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index has run to the top of its 64-day range, closing at its high on Aug 7. Nothing in the record explains the climb: the Canadian news of the window is a British Columbia wildfire that forced 20,000 evacuations, a WestJet flight attendants' strike, and a Toronto tech deal in which AMD acquired the chip startup Taalas.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index set a 63-day high on Aug 7, the same day the Senate moved on secondary tariffs against buyers of Russian oil and Trump renewed his bid to remove Fed governor Cook. Energy costs stayed elevated behind it — US diesel at $5.36 a gallon, per the Energy Information Administration — with the Strait of Hormuz still unresolved.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index reached the top of its range on Aug 7 despite a run of bad news from its largest constituents: BMW is cutting 8,000 jobs worldwide, Porsche another 5,000, and Mercedes cut its sales outlook on weak China. Adidas reported strong growth thanks to the World Cup, and Commerzbank warmed to a UniCredit takeover Berlin had called a sovereignty threat.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index climbed to 8,715 on Aug 7, its high over the window and a gain of roughly 6% from the May 15 low of 7,953. The coverage here does not explain the rise.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the top of its range, its Aug 4 high of 1112 capping a 9% climb over the period and leaving the latest reading of 1111 essentially flat on the day. Shell's agreement on Aug 3 to sell its European onshore renewables business was the notable corporate move in the window.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index climbed to the top of its range on Aug 6 through a summer of political rather than commercial disruption: Italy reimposed border checks against Spain on 31 July, and Spain answered with reciprocal checks on 7 August, after roughly 72,000 people rushed the Ceuta enclave's border. Neither dispute touched trade in goods.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index closed at its 67-day high on 7 August, up about 9 percent over the window, as Italy's border dispute with Spain escalated without touching trade. Rome had suspended Schengen against Spain on 31 July after 72,000 people rushed the Ceuta enclave, and Madrid imposed reciprocal checks on 7 August. Milan-based Bending Spoons bought Airtable for $1.28bn on 4 August.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after climbing from a 15 May low of 3036 to a 5 August high of 3327, easing 0.3% on the day. The coverage in this window points at Volkswagen, where the controlling families broke board silence to press management over excess capacity — a signal to the European industrial complex Stockholm's exporters sit inside.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index sits at 4,066, roughly 8.5% below where it stood two months ago, after falling from a 4,477 high on May 8 to a 3,966 low on June 29 and recovering only partly since. Nothing in the available reporting accounts for the decline.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Israel–Iran ceasefire holds through a set date. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for the ceasefire surviving — not a forecast, and it reprices on any strike, talks or deadline.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The contract has climbed from 34% on Jul 19 to 96% on Aug 10 as the confrontation moved from strikes to bargaining: Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructure on Aug 2, and Araghchi says an Oman-brokered agreement on new Hormuz shipping lanes is in its final stages. The strait itself stays closed, with only 8 to 15 ships crossing daily.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at the next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and the rate it tracks sets the floor under borrowing costs worldwide.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The Fed held rates at 350-375 basis points on 29 July, citing elevated inflation, and signalled rates could still rise — a hawkish hold that left the no-change contract near its high. Citadel had bet on a hike into the meeting. Trump's renewed move to fire Cook has reopened the fight over Fed independence.

poly-us-x-iran-effective-ceasfire-by-aug.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Washington and Tehran reach an effective ceasefire by a set date. It trades on what people will pay for that outcome, so it reprices on each concrete step — a mediator's draft, a condition met or added — rather than on rhetoric.
poly-us-x-iran-effective-ceasfire-by-aug.recent: The move followed the Oman-brokered track: Iran set six conditions on 08-08 and added a reparations clause, then Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said a lane-definition agreement was in its final stages, with reopening still conditional on a US act. Trump had halted the attack on Iran's infrastructure on 02 August.

poly-will-mojtaba-khamenei-be-head-of-st.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Mojtaba Khamenei, son of Iran's Supreme Leader, becomes head of state within the contract's window. Traders price a succession that Iran's clerical system never formally announces in advance, so the odds move on signals rather than statements.
poly-will-mojtaba-khamenei-be-head-of-st.recent: Tehran spent the window bargaining rather than transitioning: Iran kept the Strait of Hormuz closed under six conditions with Oman mediating, added a reparations clause on 08-08, and Araghchi framed contact with Washington as messages, not negotiations. Rezaee holding both the Guards legacy and an SNSC post is the kind of internal placement these odds read.

poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the party built around Vladimir Putin, wins the largest share of seats in Russia's State Duma election. Prices move with what traders will pay for that outcome, not with polling.
poly-will-united-russia-er-gain-the-most.recent: The contract rose from 54 on Jul 12 to a high of 71 on Aug 7, firming as Moscow hardened its war position: Galuzin said Putin has ruled out any freeze of the conflict, while Ukraine struck two Russian refineries and Russia was said to be deploying 120 North Korean missiles at Voronezh.

xag.standing: A tokenised claim on physical silver, priced per troy ounce and traded around the clock. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics and brazing all compete for the same supply.
xag.recent: The series is dominated by its own volatility rather than any event in the record: a low of 29.80 on Aug 6 and a high of 63.25 two days later on Aug 8, with the latest print at 54.99 — a swing far larger than the metal itself moved, and the mark of a thin token market. The one item touching silver's demand side is Washington's polysilicon price floor, which raises solar module costs.

wiki-spain.standing: The Wikipedia country article for Spain, a member of the EU and the Schengen area with a land and sea frontier at the western entrance to the Mediterranean. Readership rises when the country is at the centre of a European story.
wiki-spain.recent: The July peak followed the Ceuta crossings: nearly 60,000 people swam around the enclave's border fence in a week, 57 bodies were recovered, and Italy responded by reimposing Schengen checks against Spain, which Madrid then matched. Attention has fallen back since as a second story, the August 12 eclipse crossing Burgos, took over.
